guide.a.customise_system: Absolutely. This is open-source software, so you have full control. You can grab the code from GitHub and host it yourself on Bunny Edge Scripting or any compatible platform. The README has deployment instructions to get you started.
guide.q.customise_for_me: Can you customise it for me?
guide.a.customise_for_me: Yes. I offer customisation at a transparent flat rate — see chobble.com/prices for current pricing. I can help you with custom features, branding, listing image design, hosting setup, or whatever you need. You'll own the code outright, and I can show you how to maintain it yourself or handle updates for you. Over 20 years building web systems means I can usually solve problems quickly and clearly.
guide.q.hosting_and_images: Do you help with hosting and images?
guide.a.hosting_and_images: Yes to both. I can set you up on your own Bunny CDN account (or another host) and handle the technical configuration. I also design listing images if you need them. Get in touch and we'll figure out exactly what you need.
guide.q.how_do_i_restore_from_a_backup: How do I restore from a backup?
guide.a.how_do_i_restore_from_a_backup: Put the target database's DB_URL and DB_TOKEN in .env. Run deno task restore <backup.zip> from a checkout of this app. The task checks the file and asks you to confirm before it deletes any data.
guide.a.are_old_backups_deleted_automati: Yes. Only the most recent backups are kept (30 by default, configurable via MAX_BACKUPS). When a new backup is created beyond that limit, the oldest is purged automatically. The Backups page shows how many you have and when the oldest will be removed. Automatic pre-migration backups count towards this limit too.
guide.q.do_backups_require_any_special_c: Do backups require any special configuration?
guide.a.do_backups_require_any_special_c: Yes. Backups require CDN storage to be configured (STORAGE_ZONE_NAME and STORAGE_ZONE_KEY). The feature is designed for remote databases (libsql://). If storage is not configured, the backup page will show a message explaining this.
guide.q.why_does_my_site_say_it_s: Why does my site say it's in read-only mode?
guide.a.why_does_my_site_say_it_s: Read-only mode is switched on by the host (not from inside the admin) and is used for two things: sites that have fallen behind on billing, and sites undergoing maintenance. While it's on, bookings are refused and the create/edit pages for listings and groups are blocked, but everything else stays viewable. If you think your site shouldn't be in read-only mode, get in touch with whoever hosts it for you.
guide.q.how_do_i_check_for_updates: How do I check for updates?
guide.a.how_do_i_check_for_updates: Go to /admin/update to see your current build date and commit. Click Check for Updates to query GitHub for the latest release. If a newer version is available, you'll see its name and version number.
guide.q.what_does_the_version_number_mea: What does the version number mean?
guide.a.what_does_the_version_number_mea: Versions use the format vYYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS — the UTC date and time the release was built, to the second. Larger timestamps are newer, and your installation compares its own build time against the latest release tag to decide whether an update is available. Because the tag is generated at build time and pushed as the git tag, the version on the update page always matches the release on GitHub.
guide.a.what_is_the_backup_feature: The Backups page (owners only, under Settings → Backups) lets you create and download full database backups. Each backup is a .zip archive containing SQL statements for every table. Backups are stored on your configured CDN storage (Bunny CDN). Restore them with the console task shown on the page.
guide.q.how_do_i_create_a_backup: How do I create a backup?
guide.a.how_do_i_create_a_backup:
Go to Backups and click Create backup now. The system exports all database tables into a .zip file and uploads it to your storage. Previous backups are listed with their timestamps and can be downloaded at any time.

A very large database cannot be backed up from that page. One page request only allows a limited number of database calls. The page tells you when that happens. Backups can still be made from a checkout of this app with deno task backup.
guide.q.what_is_the_encryption_key_shown: What is the encryption key shown on the backup page?
guide.a.what_is_the_encryption_key_shown: The encryption key is needed if you ever restore a backup to a different site. All personal data in the database is encrypted at the field level, so you need the same encryption key to read it. Store this key securely — it cannot be recovered if lost.
guide.q.how_do_i_install_an_update: How do I install an update?
guide.a.how_do_i_install_an_update: If an update is available and your server has BUNNY_API_KEY and BUNNY_SCRIPT_ID configured, an Update Now button appears. Click it to download and deploy the new version automatically via Bunny CDN. The update is logged in the activity log. If the Bunny environment variables are not set, you'll need to deploy the update manually.
guide.q.where_can_i_read_the_release_not: Where can I read the release notes?
guide.a.where_can_i_read_the_release_not: The update page includes a link to the release notes on GitHub, where you can see what changed in each version before deciding to update.
guide.q.customise_table_columns: How do I customise which columns appear in tables?
guide.a.customise_table_columns:
Open Advanced settings. Find Listing table columns or Attendee table columns. Enter a comma-separated list of Liquid tags. The list controls which columns appear and their order.

For example, use these tags to show only the name and status in the listings table:

{{name}}, {{status}}

Clear the field to restore the default column order.
guide.q.listing_table_columns: What listing table columns are available?
guide.q.attendee_table_columns: What attendee table columns are available?
guide.q.column_format_filters: Can I use custom date or currency formatting?
guide.a.column_format_filters:
Yes. Date and price columns support Liquid filters. Add a pipe (|) after the column name. Then add the filter:

{{created | date: "%B %d, %Y"}}
{{date | date: "%A %e %b"}}
{{price | currency}}

The date filter uses strftime format codes. These are common codes:

  • %Y is the full year. %y is the two-digit year.
  • %B is the full month name. %b is the short month name.
  • %d is the day with a leading zero. %e is the day without a leading zero.
  • %A is the full weekday name. %a is the short weekday name.
  • %H is the hour in 24-hour time. %I is the hour in 12-hour time. %M is the minutes.

The currency filter shows a number in your chosen currency. For example, 2500 becomes £25.00.

Other columns, such as name and email, ignore filters. They always show their usual content.
guide.table_columns.attendee_hidden: A column is hidden when no attendee has data for it. For example, the {{email}} column is hidden when no attendee has an email address. This happens even when the column is in the template.
guide.table_reference.label: Label
guide.a.what_is_servicing: Servicing records non-customer use of your capacity — maintenance and operational jobs like a boiler service, deep clean or private hire. A service event holds a number of capacity slots on one or more listings for a date (so those slots can't be sold) and records what the job costs. Manage them under Servicing.
guide.q.create_service_event: How do I create a service event?
guide.a.create_service_event: Go to Servicing → New service event. Give it a name (the job), a start date and duration, then enter a Quantity against each listing it should block — at least one. Those slots are held for that date so they can't be double-booked. Service events appear on the dashboard's Upcoming service events list and are tagged Service in attendee tables.
guide.q.record_servicing_costs: How do I record what a service event cost?
guide.a.record_servicing_costs:
Open the service event. Select Record service event cost. Enter an Amount and an optional Note. Choose the held Listing for the cost.

Service event costs are listed below. You can edit each cost later. A double-click or refresh will not record the cost twice.
guide.q.servicing_and_profit: How do service event costs affect a listing's figures?
guide.a.servicing_and_profit:
A service event cost belongs to the listing you choose. It reduces that listing's profit. Profit is income minus service event costs.

Editing a cost adds a correction instead of replacing the first amount. The total includes the first amount and all later corrections.
guide.q.custom_css: Can I add my own CSS?
guide.a.custom_css: Yes. On the Advanced Settings page, find Custom CSS, enter your styles in the CSS box, then Save Custom CSS. It's served from /custom.css and loaded on every page after the default stylesheet, so you can tweak colours, fonts and spacing. It's cached for up to an hour, so changes can take a little while to appear everywhere.
guide.a.what_is_logistics: Logistics is for listings an agent handles at the customer's location — deliveries, equipment hire, transport, or set-up and teardown. Turn it on with the Logistics toggle in Settings → Logistics. Once enabled, listings gain a Needs logistics option and you can manage logistics agents.
guide.a.logistics_agents: Agents are the vans, drivers, or crew you assign to a booking's start and end — for example a delivery and a collection. You manage them on the Logistics page, giving each a name such as "Van 1". Assign users to an agent so they can see that agent's jobs on the deliveries page; deleting an agent clears it from any bookings it was assigned to.
guide.q.enable_logistics_on_listing: How do I turn on logistics for a listing?
guide.a.enable_logistics_on_listing: Tick Needs logistics on the listing — the option only appears once logistics is enabled. Bookings for that listing then gain start and end agent selectors and times on the attendee's Logistics tab, along with a delivery address and a pinned map location, and they show up on the deliveries run sheet.
guide.q.charge_delivery_by_area: How do I charge delivery by area?
guide.a.charge_delivery_by_area:
Set one price for each area you deliver to. The buyer picks their area on the booking form. The area's price is added to what they pay.

  1. Create a question such as "Which delivery area?", with one answer per area — for example "Zone 1" and "Zone 2". Assign the question to the listings you deliver.
  2. Open Modifiers and add a modifier for each area. Set the trigger to Question answer, tick the answer for that area, and give it a fixed charge with the area's price.
  3. Set Max times per order to 1 on the modifier. The fee is charged once per booking, not for every ticket.

The price comes from the area the buyer picks, not from their postcode — like a price list, not a distance calculation. Leave Max times per order blank. The price then works like a per-person delivery charge. Set a modifier's scope when the charge must apply to only some listings.
guide.q.delivery_address_lookup: How do customers fill in their delivery address?
guide.a.delivery_address_lookup:
Customers can search for their postcode and pick their address from a list, instead of typing it out. On the Advanced Settings page, find Address lookup. Choose a lookup provider and enter the API key from your account with them. The key stays on this server, and searches are cached to keep your provider usage down.

The search box appears when a listing collects an address, and on the admin attendee forms. The address then shows on the booking's Logistics tab. The map pin is not set by the customer. To pin the exact spot, search by postcode on the Logistics tab, or type the coordinates yourself.
guide.q.delivery_run_sheet: What is the deliveries run sheet?
guide.a.delivery_run_sheet: The deliveries page lists the drop-offs and collections for the agents a user drives, grouped by day (today and tomorrow). Each booking shows the name, listing, address (with map links), phone, and ticket token, then each job — Drop-off or Collection, with its time and agent — and a Mark done button. Owners and managers open it from the Calendar menu and can view any date; agent-only users see just this page, fixed to today and tomorrow.
guide.a.what_is_image_library: The image library holds images you upload once and reuse across listings, groups, and site pages. Each image has a name and optional alt text (a short description read by screen readers). The library needs file storage to be configured; until it is, the page shows "File storage is not configured".
guide.q.add_image_to_library: How do I add an image?
guide.a.add_image_to_library: Choose Add Image, give it a name, add optional alt text, and pick a JPEG, PNG or WebP file up to 32 MB. Each upload is automatically converted to web-optimised WebP in a full-size and a thumbnail version, so you don't need to resize images yourself.
guide.q.link_image_to_listing: How do I put an image on a listing?
guide.a.link_image_to_listing: Two ways: from an item's own Images tab you can select existing library images or upload a new one; or from an image's Edit page you can tick the listings and groups (and, for site editors, news posts and pages) to attach it to. The same image can be linked to as many items as you like.
guide.q.delete_library_image: What happens when I delete an image?
guide.a.delete_library_image: Because images are shared rather than owned by one item, deleting one removes it from every listing and page that uses it. You confirm by typing the image's name. Images used by public site content (news or pages) can only be edited or deleted by site editors.
guide.a.what_are_attendee_statuses: Statuses are labels you give a booking, such as "Confirmed". Manage them in Settings → Attendee Statuses, where you can add, rename, reorder, and delete them. Every attendee has exactly one status, shown on their attendee page. A new site starts with a single status called Confirmed.
guide.q.status_flags: What do the Public, Paid and Reservation flags mean?
guide.a.status_flags:
Each status can carry flags:

  • Public default — the status new public bookings start in (only one status can hold this). It does not control whether anything is shown publicly.
  • Paid — the status an attendee moves to automatically once their outstanding balance is paid off (only reservations advance to it).
  • Reservation — marks a deposit-now, pay-the-balance-later status; the deposit comes from the reservation amount.

A paid status can't also be a reservation, and there is only ever one public default and one paid default.
guide.q.reservation_amount: How does the reservation deposit amount work?
guide.a.reservation_amount: The deposit amount only applies to reservation statuses. Enter 10 for a flat amount across the order, 10% for a percentage of the order total, 10x to charge per item booked, or 0 for no deposit (the attendee reserves now and pays in full later).
guide.q.assign_change_status: How do I set or change an attendee's status?
guide.a.assign_change_status: New public bookings are given the public-default status automatically. To change it, use the status dropdown on the attendee's Edit tab. You can't delete a status that attendees are currently using, the last remaining status, or the current public or paid default — reassign those first.
guide.q.what_is_attendees_list: What does the Attendees page show?
guide.a.what_is_attendees_list: The Attendees page is a read-only roster of every booking across all your listings, with one row per attendee. Filter it by listing (or listing type) and sort newest or oldest first, then page through with Previous and Next. To manage a single listing's attendees, open that listing instead.
guide.q.export_attendees_csv: How do I export the attendee list?
guide.a.export_attendees_csv: Use the Export CSV link on the Attendees page. It exports every booking that matches the current filter across all pages — not just the rows visible on screen — including contact details, quantity, amount paid, check-in state, and ticket links.
guide.q.where_are_attendee_actions: Where do I edit, refund, check in or delete an attendee?
guide.a.where_are_attendee_actions: The Attendees roster is view-only. Open an individual attendee to reach the Actions tab, where you can refund, resend the confirmation, send a text, merge duplicates, or delete them; edit their details and listings on the Edit tab. Checking attendees in is done from a listing's own attendee list or the QR scanner.
